text:
Michael Misa is 19, the second pick of the 2025 draft, and playing beside Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith on San Jose's top line since Igor Chernyshov got hurt. His minutes are up more than two a night over his last ten games, and he's answered with three goals, including the snap shot that opened the scoring in Dallas on Nov. 7. Ten points in 20 games is close to what we'd expect, and nothing in his finishing looks lucky.

The part to watch is the other end. The Sharks get only 39.5% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, worse than the team without him, and the Sharks give up more expected goals per 60 than anyone. His history is loud: 62 goals in his last OHL season and the E.J. McGuire Award. Forwards picked first to fourth since 2005 have all reached 200 games when given four seasons, with a median 0.56 points a game in their first full season. Misa is at 0.50. And he has a sense of humour: asked about Yaroslav Askarov stacking the pads, Misa said, as Sharks Hockey Digest's Max Miller posted it: "I told him to do that."
